subject: Per-tenant E2E latency & cost sampling proposal
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in per-tenant cost/tail latency — proposal for sampled per-tenant telemetry

Team,

Quick note from the ops side — over the last 48 hours we've seen recurrent cost spikes (tokens billed) and 95/99th tail latency increases tied to requests on the /v1/chat/generate endpoint for Acme Data (see attached metrics snapshot). The pattern looks model-version specific and concentrated on a handful of tenants, but current console views only show aggregated route-level metrics which makes root cause slow.

Proposal (small, scoped):
- Add a lightweight sampled telemetry path that captures per-request: tenant_id, route, model_version, token_count, latency_ms, batch_size, and quantization_profile.
- Sample rate: start at 1% of requests per route, configurable by tenant and route.
- Surface the samples in a temporary "per-tenant sampler" dashboard with the ability to filter by tenant, model_version, and time window (1h/6h/24h).
- Add alerting hooks for 95th/99th latency and per-tenant token cost > baseline x2 for 10m windows.

Why small-scope: we don't need full retention or all requests long-term. This is for short-term diagnostics and rapid iteration while we evaluate longer-term metric changes. Expected storage impact at 1% sampling is minimal.

Deliverables I'd like to see in sprint:
- Sampling config (how to opt tenants/routes in/out)
- Dashboard mock (attached) + query definitions
- Short alerting playbook for CS (what to do when triggered)

Attachments: p0_metrics_snapshot.csv, sampling-dashboard-mock.png

Can you confirm feasibility and rough ETA? If we can turn something on quickly it will help our conversation with Acme (they're asking for evidence and mitigations).

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 10:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in per-tenant cost/tail latency — proposal for sampled per-tenant telemetry

Thanks Camila — this is actionable and the scope looks reasonable. A couple of clarifying Qs before we commit: 

1) Retention window: do you want sampled rows kept for 7/30/90 days? For diagnostics 7–14 days is likely enough and keeps cost down.
2) Implementation: we can implement sampling server-side in the routing layer (preferred, consistent sampling) or in the runtime before tokenization (lower overhead for logs). Server-side is easiest to associate with tenant/route. Any preference?
3) Identity: will tenant_id be available in the routing context for all requests (including legacy token flows)? If not we'll need a small mapping table.
4) Alerting thresholds: do you want absolute ms thresholds or relative (% increase from baseline)? I suggest baseline-relative for multi-model/tenant fairness; but keep an absolute floor for user experience.

Notes:
- We should avoid sampling requests with PII-heavy payloads by default; the sampling layer must respect the existing PII filter.
- If we add model_version and quant_profile, that helps immediate triage (we've seen quantization regressions cause token count increases).

I'll draft a quick spec and attach INF-3245 so we can track implementation. If we do server-side sampling it'll be a low-risk feature toggle we can enable per-tenant.

-Markus
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in per-tenant cost/tail latency — proposal for sampled per-tenant telemetry

Agree we should move on this. Please keep the first iteration deliberately narrow: 1% sample rate, 7-day retention, server-side sampling in routing. Key asks from product/CS:
- Dashboard must expose per-tenant token-cost breakdowns (tokens * cost-per-token-profile) and 95/99 latency by tenant/model_version.
- Include batch_size and quant_profile in the sample schema so we can quickly map to backend config.
- Playbook: automatic ticket creation to CS when per-tenant token cost > baseline x2 for 15 minutes and 95th latency > 1.5x baseline.

Marissa — can you coordinate with CS to define the baseline and who owns escalation?
Karthik — would you be able to slot an initial spike-sampler prototype in Telemetry team's next sprint? If not, we'll need to re-prioritize. Also flag if we need an SLA exception for the temporary retention increase.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in per-tenant cost/tail latency — proposal for sampled per-tenant telemetry

Thanks all — good alignment. I'll take ownership of scoping and the roadmap slot. Summary and immediate plan: 

- Scope: server-side sampling at 1% with a 7-day retention by default. Sample schema: tenant_id, timestamp, route, model_version, token_count, latency_ms, batch_size, quant_profile, request_id. Respect PII filter (exclude request bodies).
- ETA: prototype by end of next sprint (demo on Tue sprint demo). Production toggle and dashboard in following sprint (tentative 2-week cadence).
- Implementation ticket: INF-3245 (spec attached: INF-3245-spec.md). I'll create a short playbook and link to the HubSpot account for Acme (see link).
- Telemetry squad will canary on 5 internal tenants, then enable for Acme under a controlled flag.

Action items: 
- Markus: please draft the sampling patch and include safe-guards (PII filter + opt-out). Link PR to INF-3245.
- Camila: confirm the 5 internal tenants for canary and provide the baseline numbers (tokens/sec and 95th latency).
- Marissa: own CS playbook and escalation contact list; we need a single on-call to triage alerts during the first 72 hours.

I'll also ask infra if we need a temporary retention SLA exception; expect update by EOD Monday.

Links & attachments: INF-3245 (https://rwd.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3245), playbook draft (Drive link), p0_metrics_snapshot.csv

-Karthik
Head of Observability & Platform
Redwood Inference
